questions.stem: Match each animal to its home.
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water and a monkey lives in trees. An earthworm lives under the ground. A bird flies in the sky.

questions.stem: An animal that lives in trees is…
questions.explanation: Arboreal means living in trees. Aquatic means living in water. Fossorial means living under the ground.

questions.stem: A habitat is the ___ of a plant or an animal.
questions.explanation: A habitat is the home of a living thing. It gives food, water, air and shelter.

questions.stem: A fish can live on dry land.
questions.explanation: A fish needs water to breathe and swim. Its habitat is a pond, a river or the sea.

questions.stem: Where does each animal live? Sort them.
questions.explanation: Fish and frogs live in water. Monkeys and parrots live in trees. Earthworms and rats dig and live under the ground.

questions.stem: Which animals are aquatic? They live in water. Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Crabs, frogs, ducks and fish all live in or near water. A cow lives on the land and a monkey lives in trees.

questions.stem: Put the homes in order from the highest to the lowest.
questions.explanation: Birds fly in the sky. Monkeys live in trees. Cows walk on the ground. Earthworms live under the ground.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: the home of a living thing
questions.explanation: These five words help us name where animals live.

questions.stem: How does a pond help a frog?
options: Water to swim in and insects to eat.
Branches to climb and sleep on.
Soil to dig a tunnel in.
questions.explanation: A pond gives a frog water to swim in, insects to eat and plants to hide under. Climbing branches is what a monkey needs.

questions.stem: Birds, bats and butterflies live in the sky. This is the ___ habitat.
questions.explanation: Aerial means in the air and sky. Birds, bats and butterflies fly there.

questions.stem: A habitat gives a living thing food, water, air and shelter.
questions.explanation: A good habitat meets all the needs of the plants and animals that live there.

questions.stem: Look at the pond. Which number is the frog?
questions.image_alt: A pond with the Sun, air and clouds, a duck, a fish, water, a rock, water plants and a frog, each with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 8 is the frog. Number 4 is the fish, 7 is the water plants and 2 is the air and clouds.

questions.stem: Look at the pond. Which numbers show animals? Choose all that are right.
questions.image_alt: A pond with the Sun, air and clouds, a duck, a fish, water, a rock, water plants and a frog, each with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 3 is a duck, 4 is a fish and 8 is a frog. Number 5 is water and 6 is a rock, so they are not animals.

questions.stem: Look at the Sundarbans tree. What are its roots standing in?
questions.image_alt: A mangrove tree with breathing roots and prop roots in salty mud.
questions.explanation: Mangrove trees in the Sundarbans grow in salty mud. Their roots stand in the mud and hold the tree up.

questions.stem: Tuli goes by boat in the haor in Sylhet. She sees many fish and ducks. What kind of habitat is this?
questions.explanation: A haor is a big wetland full of water. Fish and ducks live there, so it is an aquatic habitat.

questions.stem: Anika visits a pond with her class to count the animals. What is the safe way?
options: Reach into the water to catch them.
Look with her teacher and do not touch.
questions.explanation: We look, count and do not touch. Staying with a grown-up near water keeps us safe and does not harm the animals.

questions.stem: Moung wants to see an earthworm in the garden. Where should he look?
options: in the soil under a stone
questions.explanation: Earthworms live in the soil under the ground. They are fossorial animals.

questions.stem: The Sundarbans has land, trees, water, holes in the mud and sky. It has every kind of habitat.
questions.explanation: Tigers and deer walk on land. Monkeys climb trees. Fish and crocodiles swim in the rivers. Crabs dig holes in the mud. Birds fly above.

questions.stem: Why can a fish not live in a tree?
questions.model_answer: A fish needs water to breathe and swim. A tree has no water.
questions.explanation: A fish needs water to breathe and swim. A tree is a habitat for monkeys and parrots, not for fish.

questions.stem: Crabs dig holes in the mud in the Sundarbans. A hole under the ground is a ___ habitat.
questions.explanation: Fossorial means living under the ground. Crabs, earthworms and rats use holes in the ground.

questions.stem: Anika sees a monkey eating fruit in a tree. What does the tree give the monkey? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: A tree gives a monkey fruit to eat, branches to climb and a place to sleep. A monkey does not swim or dig.

questions.stem: Class 1 counted animals in 5 minutes. Pond: 4 frogs and 6 fish. Garden: 9 ants and 3 butterflies. Which place had more animals?
questions.explanation: The pond had 4 + 6 = 10 animals. The garden had 9 + 3 = 12 animals. The garden had 2 more.

questions.stem: A kingfisher sits on a branch by a pond. It flies over the water and dives in to catch a fish. Which habitats does it use? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: The kingfisher flies in the sky, rests in a tree and hunts in the pond. It does not live under the ground.

questions.stem: Ants walk on the land and dig homes in the soil. Which two words fit their habitats?
questions.explanation: Terrestrial means on land and fossorial means under the ground. An animal can live in more than one habitat.
